title: YouTube star Hank Green says he's relied 'too heavily' on AI in an apology to fans
excerpt: Hank Green, one of YouTube's most prolific stars, is facing backlash for relying on AI to create his content.
content_html:
By Lauren Edmonds

You're currently following this author! Want to unfollow? Unsubscribe via the link in your email.

Hank Green, one of the internet's most steadfast and reliable content creators, said he's slowing down production after fans criticized him for using AI.

In addition to his personal account, Green hosts the educational YouTube channels SciShow and Crash Course. SciShow is a collection of YouTube channels focused on different scientific disciplines, while Crash Course offers videos that break down topics like Latin American literature and reading statistics.

He also created the Vlogbrothers YouTube channel with his brother, John Green. Green said in a lengthy Reddit comment on Friday that fans can expect fewer YouTube videos for the foreseeable future.

"Expect less hankschannel. It may need to pause for a while," Green wrote. "It may be that Hankschannel comes back with writing and research support. It may be that it comes back with just way fewer videos."

Green said SMUSH and 4x3, two online daily word games he produces, will be paused.

The fresh discourse surrounding Green's use of AI was sparked earlier that day on X, where he told users he had used OpenAI's ChatGPT to research a script. The revelation shocked some X users, who suggested that Green undermined his credibility by using AI without disclosing it to viewers.

As tensions grew on X, Green deleted that post and pivoted to Reddit to address the situation. He told Redditors he's "mortified" that he's "let so many people down."

"I have been relying too heavily on AI as a research aid. It can be very useful for this task, giving me access to a lot of papers I didn't know existed really fast, but I think that has been to the detriment of my work because it has not given me the freedom to find all of my own ways into and around a topic," Green said.

As tech companies push AI to become a ubiquitous part of daily life, critics have voiced concern that it could impact critical thinking skills. In 2025, a survey published by Workday found that nearly half of respondents worried the tech would cause a decline in critical thinking.

There are also concerns around mental health. OpenAI is facing several lawsuits related to users' mental health, including those that say the chatbot encouraged suicide. In June, a coalition of states launched an investigation into ChatGPT's impact on young users.

AI hallucinations, or when LLMs generate inaccurate outputs, are another problem. They've begun popping up in court documents, forcing lawyers and law firms to apologize for including false or misleading information. They've also shown up in reports from some of the world's largest consulting firms.

Green said he uses AI to find resources to research different topics. He said, however, that fans deserve to know when his words are his own or a chatbot's.

"I've been moving so fast that my own process isn't actually clear to me and I want to have it be a guarantee moving forward," Green said.

Green told fans that he's not anti-AI but understands some of their concerns, such as how the tech is trained, its environmental implications, and the consolidation of economic power by tech companies. He ultimately apologized.

"It is very likely that you (the reader) and I disagree on how or even whether AI should be used," Green said. "I think it makes sense for that disagreement to exist. But I have also always believed that my audience is more likely to be right than I am. You know what this feels like in a way I can't. And I am so sorry for diluting myself in this way and harming the thing that we have all built together."

In the post, Green said he feels pressure when creating content and will strive to manage himself more effectively. He'll also address his interactions with AI, which he described as unhealthy.

"But mostly I need to come to terms with the fact that the level of dopamine I've been getting from interacting with LLMs...with doing more and more and more and more...is not healthy for me or good for the world," Green said. "It is careless, and has disconnected me from where people are on this."

content_html_zh:
作者：Lauren Edmonds 您目前正在关注该作者！ 想要取消关注吗？ 通过电子邮件中的链接取消订阅。

汉克·格林是互联网上最坚定、最可靠的内容创作者之一，他表示，在粉丝批评他使用人工智能后，他正在放慢制作速度。

除了他的个人帐户外，Green 还主持 YouTube 教育频道 SciShow 和 Crash Course。 SciShow 是专注于不同科学学科的 YouTube 频道集合，而 Crash Course 则提供详细介绍拉丁美洲文学和阅读统计等主题的视频。

他还与他的兄弟 John Green 创建了 Vlogbrothers YouTube 频道。 格林周五在 Reddit 上发表长篇评论时表示，在可预见的未来，粉丝们预计 YouTube 视频将会减少。

“预计汉克斯频道会减少。 它可能需要暂停一段时间，”格林写道。 “汉克斯频道可能会带着写作和研究支持回来。 回归后的视频可能会少得多。”

格林表示，他制作的两款每日在线文字游戏 SMUSH 和 4x3 将被暂停。

当天早些时候，围绕 Green 使用人工智能的新讨论在 X 上引发，他告诉用户他已经使用 OpenAI 的 ChatGPT 来研究脚本。 这一消息震惊了一些 X 用户，他们认为格林在未向观众透露的情况下使用人工智能，损害了他的可信度。

随着 X 上的紧张局势加剧，格林删除了该帖子并转向 Reddit 来解决这一问题。 他告诉 Reddit 用户，他“让很多人失望”，他感到“羞愧”。

“我一直过于依赖人工智能作为研究辅助手段。 它对于这项任务非常有用，让我能够快速获得许多我不知道的论文，但我认为这对我的工作不利，因为它没有让我自由地找到进入和围绕某个主题的所有自己的方式，”格林说。

随着科技公司推动人工智能成为日常生活中无处不在的一部分，批评者表示担心它可能会影响批判性思维技能。 2025 年，Workday 发布的一项调查发现，近一半的受访者担心该技术会导致批判性思维能力下降。

人们还担心心理健康问题。 OpenAI 正面临多起与用户心理健康相关的诉讼，其中包括那些称聊天机器人鼓励自杀的诉讼。 6 月，多个州联盟发起了一项调查 ChatGPT 对年轻用户的影响。

人工智能幻觉，或者法学硕士生成不准确的输出，是另一个问题。 它们已经开始出现在法庭文件中，迫使律师和律师事务所因包含虚假或误导性信息而道歉。 它们还出现在一些世界上最大的咨询公司的报告中。

格林说，他使用人工智能来寻找资源来研究不同的主题。 不过他说，粉丝们应该知道他的话是他自己说的还是聊天机器人说的。

“我的行动太快了，以至于我自己的流程实际上并不清楚，我希望它成为前进的保证，”格林说。

格林告诉粉丝，他并不反对人工智能，但理解他们的一些担忧，例如技术如何训练、其对环境的影响以及科技公司对经济实力的巩固。 他最终道歉了。

格林说：“你（读者）和我很可能在如何甚至是否应该使用人工智能方面存在分歧。” “我认为这种分歧的存在是有道理的。 但我也一直相信我的听众比我更有可能是正确的。 你知道这是什么感觉，但我却做不到。 我很抱歉以这种方式淡化了自己，并伤害了我们共同建立的东西。”

格林在帖子中表示，他在创作内容时感到压力，会努力更有效地管理自己。 他还将讨论他与人工智能的互动，他称这种互动是不健康的。

“但最重要的是，我需要接受这样一个事实：我从与法学硕士的互动中获得的多巴胺水平……做得越来越多……对我来说不健康，也不对世界有好处，”格林说。 “这太粗心了，让我与人们在这件事上的看法脱节。”
